facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated Tanius to be 7 meters long and weigh 2 metric tons in 2010.
facts.quote: In 2010 Gregory S. Paul estimated the length of Tanius at 7 m and its weight at 2 MT.

facts.statement: A 2021 study estimated the weight of Tanius between 2,091 and 3,533 kilograms.
facts.quote: En 2021, el peso se estimó entre 2091 y 3533 kilogramos.

facts.statement: Tanius had a flat, elongated head with large windows above the temples and a narrow cheekbone.
facts.quote: La cabeza es más bien plana y alargada con largas ventanas en la parte superior de las sienes y un hueso cigomático angosto.

facts.statement: The spinous processes of Tanius vertebrae were 3.2 times taller than the vertebral body.
facts.quote: Las apófisis espinosas de las vértebras son altas, 3,2 veces más altas que el cuerpo vertebral.

facts.statement: The top surface of the third metatarsal bone in Tanius has a crescent moon profile.
facts.quote: La superficie superior del tercer hueso metatarsiano tiene el perfil de una luna creciente.

facts.statement: H. C. T'an discovered Tanius remains in April 1923 at Ch'ing-kang-kou village, ten kilometers southeast of Lai Yang in Shandong.
facts.quote: In April 1923, H. C. T'an discovered the remains in the east of Shandong at the village of Ch'ing-kang-kou, ten kilometres southeast of Lai Yang.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen PMU R.240 comes from the Jiangjunding Formation of the Wangshi Series, dating to the Campanian.
facts.quote: The holotype, PMU R.240, was recovered from the Jiangjunding Formation of the Wangshi Series dating from the Campanian.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen PMU R.240 was recovered from the Wangshi Formation dating to the Campanian.
facts.quote: El espécimen holotipo, PMU R.240, fue recuperado de la Formación Wangshi que data de la época del Campaniense.

facts.statement: Tanius lived in China during the Late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: It lived in the Late Cretaceous of China.

facts.statement: Tanius lived approximately 72 million years ago during the Campanian stage in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 72 millones de años, durante el Campaniense, en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: The fossil record for Tanius spans from the Coniacian to the Campanian, between 89.8 and 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Coniacian to Campanian (89.8 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Tanius lived in a fluvial to lacustrine environment within the Jiangjunding Formation.
facts.quote: The Jiangjunding Formation was deposited in a fluvial to lacustrine environment.

facts.statement: The climate where Tanius lived was generally warm and humid, though it began to dry out after the Jiangjunding Formation.
facts.quote: The climate was warm and humid during the majority of the timespan, although it was beginning to dry out after the Jiangjunding.

facts.statement: Tanius is a genus of hadrosauroid dinosaur.
facts.quote: Tanius (meaning "of Tan") is a genus of hadrosauroid dinosaur.

facts.statement: Tanius is classified within the family Hadrosauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Hadrosauridae

facts.statement: Recent analyses place Tanius as a basal member of Hadrosauridae, while others suggest it is even more basal within the broader Hadrosauroidea.
facts.quote: Algunos análisis recientes le dan a la especie una posición basal en el mismo; otros dan como resultado que sea aún más basal en el más amplio Hadrosauroidea.

facts.statement: The type species Tanius sinensis was named and described by Carl Wiman in 1929.
facts.quote: The type species, named and described in 1929 by Carl Wiman, is Tanius sinensis.

facts.statement: The genus name honors Chinese paleontologist Tan Xichou, while the species name refers to China.
facts.quote: El nombre del género es en honor del paleontólogo chino Tan Xichou ("H.C. Tan"), mientras que el nombre de la especie se refiere a China.

facts.statement: Although the original Tanius specimen was largely complete, only parts could be salvaged during excavation.
facts.quote: Although the specimen was originally rather complete, only parts could be salvaged.

facts.statement: A 2017 study by Zhang et al. determined that T. sinensis and T. chingkankouensis are valid species, while T. laiyangensis is likely invalid.
facts.quote: However, a more recent study, Zhang et al. (2017) determined that T. sinensis and T. chingkankouensis were valid species of Tanius, and that T. laiyangensis was probably not valid.

facts.statement: A 2019 study re-assessed "Tanius" laiyangensis as a member of the Asian saurolophine clade Kritosaurini.
facts.quote: Zhang et al. (2019) re-assessed "Tanius" laiyangensis as a member of the saurolophine clade Kritosaurini, the first of the clade from Asia.

facts.statement: The holotype of Tanius consists of the back of a flat, elongated skull.
facts.quote: It consists of the back of the skull, which was flat and elongated.

facts.statement: Tanius shared its environment with Pinacosaurus, Micropachycephalosaurus, intermediate sauropods, coelurosaurs, and cheloniids.
facts.quote: Taxa that lived alongside Tanius in the formation include the ankylosaur Pinacosaurus cf. grangeri; possibly the cerapodan Micropachycephalosaurus; intermediate sauropods; intermediate coelurosaurs; and intermediate cheloniids which show similarities to Nanhsiungchelyidae.

facts.statement: Multiple localities of dinosaur eggs have been identified in the same formation as Tanius.
facts.quote: Multiple localities of dinosaur eggs have also been identified.

facts.statement: Hadrosaur carcasses, including Tanius, were trapped and moved by a mudflow event before rapid burial.
facts.quote: The sediment in the location of the hadrosaur excavations was deposited by a mudflow event, where the carcasses were trapped and moved a short distance before rapid burial.

facts.statement: At least 20 individuals of hadrosaurs, including Tanius, of various ages have been uncovered.
facts.quote: At least 20 individuals of hadrosaurs have been uncovered, of various ages.

rejected.statement: The Tanius holotype was excavated in October 1923 by Austrian paleontologist Otto Zdansky.
rejected.quote: In October of the same year they were excavated by Tan's associate, the Austrian paleontologist Otto Zdansky.

rejected.statement: Research by Borinder in 2015 identified that Tanius sinensis lived from the latest Campanian to the earliest Maastrichtian.
rejected.quote: As the Hongtuya is directly older than the Jiangjunding, it was identified that Tanius sinensis lived in the latest Campanian to earliest Maastrichtian by Borinder in 2015.
